record.paper_title: Finite translation generalized quadrangles: old results, new results, open problems
record.original_question: If O is a translation generalized oval in PG(3n − 1, q) with q even—that is, a generalized oval for which there is a group of involutions fixing O and acting regularly on all elements except one distinguished element—is O necessarily regular?

evidence.quote: 2. Is any translation generalized oval regular?

Then O is a translation generalized oval, with axis the tangent space PG(i)(2n − 1, q) of O at PG(i)(n−1, q) ∈ O, if there is a group of involutions of PGL(3n, q) with axis PG(i)(2n − 1, q), fixing O and acting regularly on O − {PG(i)(n − 1, q)}.
Here, we speak of a regular pseudo-oval, respectively a regular pseudo-ovoid.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let q be an even prime power and let n ≥ 1 be an integer. A generalized oval (or pseudo-oval) in PG(3n−1, q) is a family O of q^n + 1 mutually disjoint (n−1)-dimensional subspaces of PG(3n−1, q) with the property that any three distinct members of O span the whole space PG(3n−1, q). For each element π ∈ O there is a unique (2n−1)-dimensional subspace τ_π of PG(3n−1, q), called the tangent space of O at π, which contains π and is disjoint from every other element of O.

A generalized oval O is called regular if it arises by field reduction from an oval in the projective plane PG(2, q^n), i.e., if there exists an oval Ω in PG(2, q^n) such that O is the image of Ω under the natural map PG(2, q^n) → PG(3n−1, q) given by viewing GF(q^n) as an n-dimensional vector space over GF(q).

A generalized oval O is called a translation generalized oval with axis τ_π (for some distinguished π ∈ O) if there exists a subgroup of PGL(3n, q) consisting of involutions, each fixing τ_π pointwise (i.e., having τ_π as axis), fixing the set O setwise, and acting regularly on O \ {π}.

Question: For q even, must every translation generalized oval in PG(3n−1, q) be regular?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches show ongoing work on classification of pseudo-ovals in PG(3n−1, q) for q even (including results on pseudo-ovals containing a pseudo-conic, pseudo-ovals in even characteristic via ovoidal Laguerre planes, and 2024 classification work in small orders), and partial regularity results such as elementarity when every element induces a Desarguesian spread. However, no source clearly states that the general question — whether every translation generalized oval in PG(3n−1, q) with q even is necessarily regular — has been settled. The status is therefore not conclusively determined from the available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Pseudo-ovals in even characteristic and ovoidal Laguerre planes
status_evidence.snippet: A pseudo-(hyper)oval in PG(3n-1, q), q even, n prime, such that every element induces a Desarguesian spread, is elementary.
status_evidence.claim: Partial regularity results exist under additional spread assumptions, but not the unconditional translation case.

status_evidence.title: Classifying pseudo-ovals, translation generalized quadrangles, and elation Laguerre planes of small order
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of pseudo-ovals in PG(3n-1,2) for n=3,4 and in PG(3n-1,q) for n=5,6 (with one associated plane Desarguesian).
status_evidence.claim: Only small-order or restricted classifications are known; the general translation case is not resolved here.

status_evidence.title: Translation Generalized Quadrangles in Even Characteristic
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizations of classical generalized quadrangles in even characteristic.
status_evidence.claim: Related characterizations exist but do not explicitly resolve the translation generalized oval regularity question.
